units.name: cpp-core
units.role: Owns the wire connection to a drone/GCS: transports, MAVLink framing, and the Mavsdk/System handle objects everything else is built on.
units.description: This is the foundation of the whole SDK. It knows how to open a UDP, TCP or serial link to a drone or ground station, speak the raw MAVLink protocol over it, and keep track of which 'systems' (vehicles) have shown up on the link. Every other language binding and every plugin ultimately calls down into this layer to actually talk to hardware.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk
entrypoints.plain: The top-level object an application creates to start using MAVSDK; owns all connections and discovered systems.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk::Mavsdk
entrypoints.plain: Constructs a new Mavsdk instance from a Configuration.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk::add_any_connection
entrypoints.plain: Opens a UDP/TCP/serial link described by a URL string such as udp://:14540.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk::systems
entrypoints.plain: Returns the list of vehicles/ground-stations currently seen on the connections.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk::first_autopilot
entrypoints.plain: Blocks until an autopilot system shows up (or a timeout elapses) and returns it.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk::subscribe_on_new_system
entrypoints.plain: Registers a callback that fires whenever a new vehicle/system is discovered.

entrypoints.name: System
entrypoints.plain: Represents one discovered vehicle or ground station; plugins are attached to a System.

entrypoints.name: ServerComponent
entrypoints.plain: Represents this program's own identity on the MAVLink network, used by *_server plugins that emulate a vehicle/component.

effects.description: Opens UDP and TCP sockets to send/receive MAVLink packets (udp_connection.cpp, tcp_client_connection.cpp, tcp_server_connection.cpp), and makes HTTP requests via curl (curl_wrapper.cpp) to fetch things like camera definition XML.
Opens and configures serial ports (termios raw mode) to talk to autopilots over USB/UART (serial_connection.cpp).
Reads and writes a local file cache directory for downloaded artifacts, and receives/sends files over MAVLink FTP (file_cache.cpp, mavlink_ftp_server.cpp, mavlink_ftp_client.cpp).
Reads steady/system clock time for timestamps, timeouts and time-sync with the vehicle (mavsdk_time.cpp).
Generates random temporary file/directory names for the file cache using std::random_device/mt19937 (fs_utils.cpp).

units.name: cpp-plugins
units.role: The per-capability drone APIs (Action, Telemetry, Camera, Mission, ...) that application code actually programs against.
units.description: Once a connection exists (via cpp-core), a developer picks the capability they need — arming and flying (Action), reading sensor data (Telemetry), controlling a camera (Camera/CameraServer), uploading a mission, and around three dozen others — and instantiates the matching plugin class attached to a System or ServerComponent. Each plugin's public header is auto-generated from a shared MAVSDK-Proto definition so client and server behave consistently across all languages.

entrypoints.name: Action
entrypoints.plain: Client-side API for arming, taking off, landing and other flight commands.

entrypoints.name: Action::arm
entrypoints.plain: Arms the vehicle's motors.

entrypoints.name: Action::disarm
entrypoints.plain: Disarms the vehicle's motors.

entrypoints.name: Action::takeoff
entrypoints.plain: Commands the vehicle to take off.

entrypoints.name: Telemetry
entrypoints.plain: Client-side API for subscribing to vehicle sensor/state data such as position and battery.

entrypoints.name: Telemetry::subscribe_position
entrypoints.plain: Registers a callback invoked every time a new GPS position is received.

entrypoints.name: Telemetry::position
entrypoints.plain: Returns the most recent known position.

entrypoints.name: CameraServer
entrypoints.plain: Server-side API letting this program pretend to be a camera component on the MAVLink network.

entrypoints.name: CameraServer::subscribe_take_photo
entrypoints.plain: Registers a callback fired when a client asks this simulated camera to take a photo.

entrypoints.name: CameraServer::respond_take_photo
entrypoints.plain: Sends back the result of a take-photo request.

effects.description: Some plugins write downloaded/cached data to local disk, e.g. LogFiles saves flight logs (log_files_impl.cpp), Camera caches the camera definition XML (camera_impl.cpp/camera_definition.cpp), and ComponentMetadata caches component metadata files (component_metadata_impl.cpp).

units.name: mavsdk-server
units.role: A standalone gRPC daemon that wraps cpp-core + cpp-plugins so that non-C++ clients (Python's gRPC client, Swift, etc.) can drive MAVSDK over the network.
units.description: This is a separate executable process. It links the C++ core library and every plugin, and for each plugin exposes an equivalent gRPC service (generated from the same proto files as the plugin itself), listening on a local TCP port. A client anywhere that speaks gRPC — most notably py/mavsdk's older grpc mode and other language SDKs not vendored in this repo — can connect to it instead of linking C++ directly.

entrypoints.name: main
entrypoints.plain: Process entrypoint of the mavsdk_server binary.

entrypoints.name: GrpcServer
entrypoints.plain: Owns the gRPC server instance and registers every plugin's service implementation on it.

entrypoints.name: GrpcServer::setup_port
entrypoints.plain: Binds the gRPC server to a local TCP port (insecure/local by default).

effects.description: Listens on a local TCP port for incoming gRPC connections (grpc::ServerBuilder::AddListeningPort in grpc_server.cpp).

units.name: c-bindings
units.role: A plain-C API (libcmavsdk) that wraps the C++ core and plugins so non-C++ runtimes (ctypes, other FFIs) can call MAVSDK.
units.description: C++ has no stable ABI, so anything that isn't C++ (like Python's ctypes) can't call cpp-core directly. This layer is a thin extern "C" shim: for every plugin and for the core Mavsdk/System classes it exposes plain C functions and opaque handles that internally construct and call the real C++ objects. Almost all of it is generated from the same proto definitions as the C++ plugins, so it stays in lockstep with them automatically.

entrypoints.name: mavsdk_create
entrypoints.plain: C entrypoint that creates a Mavsdk instance, returned as an opaque handle.

entrypoints.name: mavsdk_add_any_connection
entrypoints.plain: C entrypoint that opens a connection URL on a Mavsdk handle.

units.name: jni-bindings
units.role: The JNI glue library (mavsdk_jni) that lets JVM code (Kotlin/Java) call into the C bindings.
units.description: This is a small native library, loaded with System.loadLibrary from the JVM side, that implements every native method the Kotlin SDK declares. Each JNI function unpacks its Java arguments, calls the matching function in c-bindings, and converts the result back into something Java/Kotlin can use, including turning native callbacks into JVM callbacks. Almost all of the per-plugin files are generated from the proto definitions, matching the pattern used by c-bindings and cpp-plugins.

entrypoints.name: Java_io_mavsdk_jni_NativeMavsdk_create
entrypoints.plain: JNI-exported native implementation backing NativeMavsdk.create on the Java side.

entrypoints.name: NativeMavsdk.create
entrypoints.plain: Java-side native method declaration for creating a Mavsdk instance from the JVM.

entrypoints.name: NativeMavsdk.addAnyConnection
entrypoints.plain: Java-side native method declaration for opening a connection from the JVM.

units.name: kotlin-sdk
units.role: The public Kotlin Multiplatform API (io.mavsdk.kotlin) that Android/JVM apps program against; a coroutine-friendly facade over jni-bindings.
units.description: This is what a Kotlin or Android developer actually imports: Mavsdk, System and one class per plugin (Action, Telemetry, Camera, ...), all exposing suspend functions and Flows instead of raw callbacks. On JVM/Android it is implemented by loading the native mavsdk_jni library and forwarding every call to the matching Native* class from jni-bindings, translating between Kotlin types and the primitive handles the native side understands.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk
entrypoints.plain: The Kotlin object an app creates to start using MAVSDK; wraps a native jni-bindings handle.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk.addAnyConnection
entrypoints.plain: Kotlin suspend-friendly wrapper that opens a connection via NativeMavsdk.addAnyConnection.

entrypoints.name: NativeLibraryLoader.loadLibrary
entrypoints.plain: Loads the mavsdk_jni native library into the JVM process (System.loadLibrary).

effects.description: Loads the native mavsdk_jni shared library into the process via System.loadLibrary before any native call can be made (NativeLibraryLoader.kt).

units.name: python-ctypes-sdk
units.role: The 'mavsdk' PyPI package: a synchronous ctypes wrapper around c-bindings, giving Python code direct in-process access to MAVSDK without a separate server.
units.description: This is a Python package that loads the compiled libcmavsdk shared library at import time and calls its C functions through ctypes. It exposes Mavsdk, System and one module per plugin, mirroring the C API one-to-one. Unlike the older gRPC approach, there is no separate mavsdk_server process involved here; the C++ core runs inside the same Python process.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk
entrypoints.plain: The Python object an app creates to start using MAVSDK; wraps a ctypes handle into libcmavsdk.

entrypoints.name: System
entrypoints.plain: Python wrapper for a discovered vehicle/system, exposing plugin accessors.

entrypoints.name: _find_library
entrypoints.plain: Locates and loads the platform-specific libcmavsdk shared library at import time.

effects.description: Searches a list of local paths for the libcmavsdk shared library and loads it via ctypes.CDLL (cmavsdk_loader.py).
setup.py imports the subprocess module as part of its packaging/build steps.

units.name: python-async-sdk
units.role: The 'aiomavsdk' PyPI package: an asyncio-friendly facade over python-ctypes-sdk for async Python applications.
units.description: This package gives Python's asyncio users an async/await API (async context managers, async generators for subscriptions) instead of the blocking calls python-ctypes-sdk exposes directly. Internally every potentially-blocking call is dispatched through an executor onto the underlying synchronous Mavsdk/System objects, so it does no work itself beyond scheduling and translating between sync and async styles.

entrypoints.name: Mavsdk
entrypoints.plain: Async wrapper an app creates to start using MAVSDK with asyncio; delegates to python-ctypes-sdk's Mavsdk.

entrypoints.name: System
entrypoints.plain: Async wrapper for a discovered vehicle/system.

effects.description: setup.py reads README.md from disk with open(...).read() to use as the package's long description.

units.name: codegen-tooling
units.role: The proto-to-source generators that keep the cpp-plugins, mavsdk-server, c-bindings, jni-bindings and kotlin-sdk plugin surfaces in sync with the MAVSDK-Proto definitions.
units.description: MAVSDK defines each plugin's API once, as a .proto file in the separate MAVSDK-Proto repository, and then generates the matching hand-review-quality source in every language from it: C++ plugin headers, gRPC service wrappers, the C API, the JNI glue and its Java native declarations, and the Kotlin accessors. This unit is the machinery that does that generation and validates its own output; it is why so many files elsewhere in this repository carry an 'AUTOGENERATED, do not edit' header.

entrypoints.name: grpc_server_jinja.main
entrypoints.plain: Renders the mavsdk_server gRPC server header/source from a Jinja template and writes them to disk.

entrypoints.name: generate_cmake.main
entrypoints.plain: Writes the CMakeLists fragment listing which plugin sources should be built, based on what was generated.

entrypoints.name: validate_generated.main
entrypoints.plain: Runs a subprocess check that generated JNI/Java sources build and match expectations.

effects.description: Writes generated source files (e.g. grpc_server.hpp/.cpp, plugins_generated.cmake) directly to the working tree of the other language directories (grpc_server_jinja.py:21,26; generate_cmake.py:16).
Shells out to run generation/build/validation commands, e.g. validate_generated.py invokes subprocess.run to build and check generated code.

units.name: repo-maintenance-tools
units.role: A standalone maintenance script for pruning old CI-published Docker Hub images; unrelated to the MAVSDK library itself.
units.description: This is a small operational script, run out-of-band from the SDK build, that logs into Docker Hub and deletes old pull-request-tagged container images past a configurable age, to keep the organization's Docker Hub storage from growing without bound.

entrypoints.name: main
entrypoints.plain: Logs into Docker Hub and deletes old pr-tagged images older than the configured max age.

effects.description: Calls the Docker Hub v2 API to log in, list, and delete image tags (DOCKER_HUB_API requests via the requests library).
Reads DOCKERHUB_USERNAME, DOCKERHUB_PASSWORD, TARGET_ORG, MAX_AGE_DAYS, TAG_PREFIX and DRY_RUN from the environment.
